agent.name: FlaskAppAgent
agent.responsibility: Create app.py. This is the Flask application with all four routes. Depends on Agent 1 having already created the database.

dependencies.dependency: flavorforge.db must exist before this app starts.

imports.import: from flask import Flask, request, render_template, render_template_string

agent.app_setup: Define app = Flask(__name__). Define a helper function get_db_connection() that returns a sqlite3.connect("flavorforge.db") connection with row_factory set to sqlite3.Row so columns are accessible by name.

route.logic: Return render_template("index.html"). No database call needed.

route.description: Adds a new recipe with ingredients and cuisine to the database.

logic.step: INSERT INTO Recipes (name, instructions) VALUES (recipe_name, '') and capture lastrowid as recipe_id.

For each ingredient in the ingredients list: - Strip whitespace. Skip if empty string. - INSERT OR IGNORE INTO Ingredients (name) VALUES (ingredient). - SELECT id FROM Ingredients WHERE name = ingredient to get ingredient_id. - INSERT OR IGNORE INTO Recipe_Ingredients (recipe_id, ingredient_id) VALUES (recipe_id, ingredient_id).

For the cuisine string: - INSERT OR IGNORE INTO Cuisines (name) VALUES (cuisine). - SELECT id FROM Cuisines WHERE name = cuisine to get cuisine_id. - INSERT OR IGNORE INTO Recipe_Cuisines (recipe_id, cuisine_id) VALUES (recipe_id, cuisine_id).

route.returns: HTML snippet string using render_template_string. Format: a single table row. Example: {recipe_name}Added

route.description: Takes a list of ingredients the user has on hand. Returns recipes ranked by how many of those ingredients they contain.

logic.step: Clean the ingredients list: strip whitespace, filter empty strings, lowercase all values.

Build a parameterized SQL query. Use a placeholder string for the IN clause based on the length of the list. Example placeholder: (?, ?, ?) for 3 ingredients.
SQL pattern: SELECT r.name, COUNT(i.name) as match_count FROM Recipes r JOIN Recipe_Ingredients ri ON r.id = ri.recipe_id JOIN Ingredients i ON ri.ingredient_id = i.id WHERE LOWER(i.name) IN ({placeholders}) GROUP BY r.id ORDER BY match_count DESC

route.returns:
HTML snippet using render_template_string. An unordered list of results. Each list item shows recipe name and match count. Example:
  • Pasta Pomodoro — 3 ingredients matched
    • If no results:
  • No matching recipes found.

route.description: Takes two cuisine names. Returns recipes that belong to BOTH cuisines simultaneously. Uses a double-join with HAVING COUNT = 2 strategy.

logic.step:
SQL pattern: SELECT r.name FROM Recipes r JOIN Recipe_Cuisines rc ON r.id = rc.recipe_id JOIN Cuisines c ON rc.cuisine_id = c.id WHERE c.name IN (cuisine_a, cuisine_b) GROUP BY r.id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT c.id) = 2
Use parameterized query: WHERE c.name IN (?, ?) with (cuisine_a, cuisine_b) as params.

route.returns:
HTML snippet using render_template_string. A div with a heading and a list of recipe names. Example:
Fusion: Italian + Indian
  • Recipe Name
If no results:

No fusion recipes found for these two cuisines.

agent.app_runner: At the bottom of app.py, under if __name__ == "__main__": Call app.run(debug=True).

validation.check: python app.py must start without errors after init_db.py has been run.
POST /add_recipe with valid form data must return a table row HTML string and persist the recipe in the db.
POST /predictive_match with ingredients that exist in seed data must return at least one list item.
POST /cultural_fusion with cuisine_a=Italian and cuisine_b=Indian must return the fusion div (may be empty list if no cross-cuisine recipes in seed data — that is acceptable).
No route should crash on empty input. Handle empty lists gracefully.
